methodology: Same NetSheetCalc/TitleTap white-label platform as the Agency Title, Inc. entry above, but a distinct tenant/company (app_id=479, a sibling-but-independent account, not a child location of Agency Title's app_id=582). Discovered via a broader netsheetcalc.com quickquote directory search (see CALCULATORS.md's 2026-08-04 Rounsavall/Indiana entry, which harvested this same operator's separate IN-scoped child tenant app_id=480 but left this KY parent tenant, app_id=479, unharvested). The old getAppData JSON endpoint returns only one hardcoded flat constant (Lender's Title Insurance Premium); the newer getNetSheetConfig endpoint (GET non-auth-ajax.php?action=getNetSheetConfig&app_id=479) reveals two additional fields are formula-driven rather than flat: 'Owner's Title Insurance' and 'Local Government Premium Tax', both referencing a tenant-specific rate-table key 'Kentucky479' resolved via the platform's public GET api/index.php/rate/<amount>/<key> endpoint (same pattern documented for Rounsavall's Indiana tenant in CALCULATORS.md). The Owner's Title Insurance formula rounds the purchase price to the nearest $1,000 and calls rate/500000/Kentucky479 -> {"rate":"1940"}. The Local Government Premium Tax formula makes a second API call using the first call's result and the selected county's raw dropdown value (format 'pt_ml@<mill-multiplier>#<id>'); reproducing the platform's own client-side formula.js logic (GET request built from the county's mill-multiplier substring, with the URL-fragment '#...' suffix stripped, matching real browser URL-parsing behavior) yields rate/1940/pt_ml@0.05 -> {"rate":"97"}, i.e. 1940 * 0.05 (Jefferson/Louisville Urban Services' 0.05 mill-multiplier) = $97.00, above the config's own $5.00 floor. No personal data required at any step. Note: the 'Owner's Title Insurance' line is conditionally displayed only when the 'Buyer paying for Owner's title insurance policy?' toggle is set to Yes (the tool's own default is No/seller-pays); the figure below was computed by directly replicating the tool's own formula/API call regardless of toggle state, consistent with how Rounsavall's Indiana tenant was harvested in this same catalog. The Lender's Title Insurance Premium and Local Government Premium Tax fields have no such toggle gate and are always computed/shown.

methodology: Classic ASP.NET WebForms + UpdatePanel app, same family as this catalog's already-documented Old Republic ortconline.com/Web2 and CT ortratecalculator.oldrepublictitle.com entries, driven with a plain requests-style session (cookie jar, no browser/JS). BASIC), txtLiabilityAmt=500000, txtCrLiabilityAmt=400000, txtStreetAddress/txtCity/txtZipCode as above, txtPolicyEffectiveDate=today's date (required; omitting it silently blanked the results panel on a first attempt), ManTyoe=rdoAddress (default 'Address Verification' tax-jurisdiction method, left as-is), and btnCalculate=Calculate clicked as a real <input type=submit> (no ScriptManager async-postback headers needed -- a plain full postback works, consistent with the 'omit async headers' lesson already documented for Knight Barry Title Group elsewhere in this catalog).
